guides.title: Build typed route URLs
guides.summary: Encode named route parameters without concatenating user input into URLs.
guides.markdown:
Use createRouteBuilder with literal patterns. Ordinary parameters accept strings. Catch-all parameters accept a nonempty array of path segments. The builder encodes each segment. It rejects unknown names, missing parameters and unsupported patterns.

This helper constructs URLs. It does not register routes, authorize requests or prove that a page exists. In an application, prefer the generated route registry when available. Keep authorization on the server. Query state has a separate URL-state API.

guides.title: Capture development navigation and RPC lifecycle evidence
guides.summary: Opt in to bounded navigation and client RPC phases without storing URLs, arguments or state values.
guides.markdown:
In Vite development code, import startDevelopmentTrace from @cossackframework/core/devtools and call it with an optional capacity (1–2048 events, default 512). Keep the returned session. Read session.snapshot() for versioned lifecycle events and call session.stop() when finished. Calls are not replayed or executed by snapshot reads.

Capture covers framework navigation and component HTTP/SSE and WebSocket proxies. Events are a discriminated union: narrow by kind (rpc or navigation) before reading operation-specific fields. Each call has a local callId, an opaque componentId and a UUID requestId when available. Phases are start, response, state-reconciled and finish. Start means a local attempt, not proof of server dispatch. State reconciliation can skip stale fields and does not prove a DOM commit. Terminal outcomes are succeeded, failed, cancelled, timeout or disconnected. Cancellation does not prove rollback or stop ignored remote work.

No arguments, returned values, state values, method names, routes, provider names or raw errors are stored. Non-UUID wire request identifiers are omitted. Snapshots are detached. dropped counts evicted events; partial histories must not be presented as complete. Times use the local wall clock and sequence gives event order. Each new session stops the old one; in-flight calls stay with the old session and are not adopted. Stopping capture does not cancel application calls and can leave an unfinished history.

Capture is disabled outside Vite development. Server-side correlation, browser UI, generated-browser acceptance and CLI/MCP trace access remain open under RT-28. This is the shared runtime foundation, not completion of those integrations.

Navigation events retain navigationId across start/cache/layouts/transition/scroll/finish. Their finish records outcome and committed. component-prepared records an app/layout/page/loading role and the same opaque componentId used by RPC events from that instance. Preparation can fail; it is not proof of a commit or of the cause of every later RPC. Global invalidations and standalone prefetch decisions use navigationId: null. Navigation callbacks retain capture ownership across awaits and stop recording after their terminal event.

Snapshots now include capturedAt and components: a weak registry of at most 64 observed instances. Component records have independent capture times and current lifecycle, initialized public/client state names, passive resource states, scope ownership/counts and transport status. These are current reads, not historical state reconstruction. Values are omitted by default. session.inspect(component, { state: ['count', 'draft'] }) selects up to 32 initialized public/client fields; private/internal/unknown fields stay excluded. Selection returns detached tagged values and is not retained in the event buffer or future default snapshots. Resources are inspected without calling getters or loaders; scope reads do not resolve services. Provider names, cursors, owner URLs, scope keys and raw errors/results are omitted.

State/resource/transport inventories have 64-entry limits; scope ancestry is limited to 16 with at most 64 service slots per scope. Values have a shared 256-node budget, depth 4, 32 object/array entries and 512-character strings. Accessors, unsupported objects, cycles, sparse holes and truncation are explicit markers. Getters and toJSON are not called, but JavaScript proxy reflection can invoke traps; do not select untrusted proxies. Known secret names and common credential strings are redacted, not every possible secret. Select only fields appropriate to inspect/share. Stopping capture stops passive reads. Tracking is unavailable on platforms without WeakRef, while explicit inspect remains available.
